leak.title: A thousand people see you. Seven come back.
leak.line1: The 993 who dropped off already cost you money. You just didn't keep them.
leak.line2: Double the ad spend and seven becomes fourteen. Give people a reason to stay and a reason to return, and the same thousand are worth three or four times as much.
leak.note: Illustrative figures, to show where the money goes. Your own numbers get worked out in the free check.

items.name: Get found
items.goal: Show up in Google search, show up on Instagram and Facebook
items.symptom: Someone nearby searches for exactly what you sell, and you're on page two — where nobody scrolls. A customer messages your Facebook page asking about a booking, and there's no WhatsApp number anywhere for them to reach you faster.

items.name: Get remembered
items.goal: A month later, they can still name you

items.name: Keep them

faq.title: The six things you are about to ask.

items.q: We don't have a Google Business Profile, or the password is with an old agency — what happens?
items.a: This is common — profiles are often set up years ago by a web developer or a former employee, and the login gets lost along the way. The free check doesn't need admin access; public information is enough. Getting management access back is something we can arrange for you, from €350, and it needs proof that you own the business. That step is decided by Google, not us, so we can't guarantee the outcome.

items.q: Can you also reach Chinese-speaking customers?
items.a: If it's relevant to your customers, yes. Every plan already includes bilingual review replies and a bilingual profile rewrite, in English and Chinese, from day one. For businesses that want a presence on Xiaohongshu specifically, to reach Dublin's Chinese-speaking community, we scope that separately — it's a smaller, more specific audience than Google or Instagram, so it's worth a quick conversation about fit rather than bundling it into every plan by default.

items.q: Is the loyalty system something you build, or something off the shelf?
items.a: It comes from the 1688.ie Essential Wangpu plan — a one-off build on your own website, so the data and the system are yours for good, not rented software. Off-the-shelf options like Square Loyalty or Smile.io switch on faster, but the monthly fee grows with your member count, your data sits on their servers, and adding a feature means waiting on their roadmap. Building it (in-house, not resold) is what the Essential Wangpu plan does; the Full cycle plan runs it day to day — scan-to-join, points redemption, the member dashboard. That's the clearest difference between us and a typical marketing agency.

items.q: I'm not in food and drink — does this still work for my business?
items.a: Yes. Clinics, salons, garages, tradespeople, solicitors and estate agents all run this. The four stages stay the same; what changes is what happens inside each one — a café's stage four is stored value and points, an estate agent's is referrals and staying in touch with past clients.

items.q: How many case studies do you have?
items.a: We're not going to try to win you over with a case-study count — numbers like that are easy to inflate and impossible for you to check. What you can check is on this page: the quality of the content ideas, how specific the free check turns out to be, the volume delivered in month one, and a live look at the loyalty back office. If month one disappoints you, the remaining months are refunded in full — that's worth more than any case study.

items.q: Can you guarantee a page-one ranking or more followers?
items.a: No, and we won't say we can. Any agency that promises that is worth a follow-up question about how — rankings and reach both sit with the platform, not with us. What we commit to is output volume and output quality, and both go in the contract.
